meta.gaugeNote: Gauge A (globalResilienceScore) is a LEADING fragility measure on a 6-18 month horizon: in a downturn three of its five pillars mechanically improve, so the composite cannot signal concurrent stress. Concurrent stress detection lives in stressGauge, which is not averaged into Gauge A.
meta.liquidityNote: Liquidity pillar redefined from discontinued Wilshire 5000 proxy to Buffett Indicator (Total Corp. Equities / GDP), percentile-scored against full history. See fetch_data.py comments.

rules.gaugeACaption: Leading fragility, 6–18 month horizon. Measures how much there is to go wrong, not whether it is going wrong now.
rules.gaugeBCaption: Concurrent stress, 0–3 month horizon. Two published triggers: the Sahm rule on real-time vintages, and the 4-quarter change in bank delinquency. This is what decides the Critical regime.

cycle.coreQuestion: Where are we in the credit cycle?
cycle.name: Cycle
cycle.scoredOnLabel: the spread itself, in percentage points

bands.label: Deeply inverted
bands.reading: Peak monetary tightening. Credit contraction has historically followed within 6–18 months.

bands.label: Inverted
bands.reading: Inversion established. Bank net interest margins compressed; lending incentive falling.

bands.label: Moderately inverted
bands.reading: Cycle peak probability elevated. Credit still flowing, but on worsening terms.

bands.label: Marginally inverted
bands.context: The entry and exit of every inversion
bands.reading: The curve sits on the boundary. Direction matters more than level here.

bands.label: Normalizing
bands.reading: Post-inversion steepening — historically the phase immediately preceding recession onset, not an all-clear.

bands.label: Late normalization
bands.reading: Steepening well under way, usually because the front end is being cut into weakness.

bands.label: Normal
bands.reading: Mid-cycle expansion. Credit conditions supportive.

bands.label: Comfortably positive
bands.reading: Expansion with a healthy term premium. Banks well compensated for maturity transformation.

bands.label: Steep
bands.reading: Early-cycle recovery. Maximum credit incentive for banks.

liquidity.coreQuestion: How large are equity claims against the economy that services them?
liquidity.name: Liquidity
liquidity.scoredOnLabel: the percentile rank of the ratio against its own history since 1945

bands.label: Bottom quintile
bands.reading: Equity capitalisation deeply depressed relative to output. Historically the best entry conditions on record.

bands.label: Well below average
bands.reading: Valuations undemanding against the size of the economy.

bands.label: Below median
bands.reading: Normal. Equity claims broadly proportionate to output.

bands.label: Above median
bands.reading: Beginning to run ahead of the real economy. Sensitivity to earnings disappointment rising.

bands.label: Elevated
bands.reading: Late-cycle territory. Returns increasingly dependent on multiple expansion rather than output growth.

bands.label: High
bands.reading: The claim on output is large enough that a normal recession implies a large repricing.

bands.label: Very high
bands.reading: Only the extremes of the record sit above here. Fragile to any liquidity withdrawal.

bands.label: Extreme
bands.reading: Top 5% of eighty years of history. Every prior visit to this band was followed by a major drawdown.

premium.coreQuestion: Are investors being compensated for taking equity risk?
premium.name: Premium
premium.scoredOnLabel: E/P minus the 10-year Treasury yield, in percentage points

bands.label: Negative
bands.context: Equities yield less than the 10-year Treasury
bands.reading: No compensation whatsoever for holding equity risk. The bond is the higher-yielding asset.

bands.label: Critically compressed
bands.reading: Effective risk parity with Treasuries. Sentinel alert active.

bands.label: Below the Sentinel threshold
bands.reading: Inside the Red Alert band. Any rate or earnings shock lands on no cushion.

bands.label: Compressed
bands.reading: Above the alert line but with little margin. Risk/return trade-off deteriorating.

bands.label: Thin
bands.reading: Compensation present but slim. Sensitive to rate moves.

bands.label: Adequate
bands.reading: Normal market functioning. Equities paid for their risk.

bands.label: Comfortable
bands.reading: Equities clearly favoured over bonds on a forward basis.

bands.label: Wide
bands.reading: Deeply attractive against bonds. Large margin of safety.

solvency.coreQuestion: Is the banking system functionally sound?
solvency.name: Solvency
solvency.scoredOnLabel: the share of all bank loans 30+ days past due

bands.label: Very low
bands.reading: Loan books performing better than at any point in the series.

bands.label: Low
bands.reading: Excellent credit quality. Banking plumbing unobstructed.

bands.label: Long-run normal, lower half
bands.reading: Normal. Losses within the range banks provision for as a matter of course.

bands.label: Long-run normal, upper half
bands.reading: Still normal, but the direction of travel starts to matter.

bands.label: Elevated
bands.reading: Credit quality deteriorating. Acceleration is the signal, not the level.

bands.label: Deteriorating
bands.reading: Provisioning rising fast enough to constrain new lending.

bands.label: Severe
bands.reading: Balance-sheet repair displaces credit extension. Systemic stress.

bands.label: Systemic
bands.reading: Government intervention has historically been required from here.

debt.name: Debt
debt.scoredOnLabel: debt payments as a share of disposable personal income

bands.label: Low
bands.reading: Ample disposable income after debt service. Consumer can absorb an income shock.

bands.label: Healthy
bands.reading: Balance sheets well positioned.

bands.label: Normal
bands.reading: Within the post-crisis range. No constraint on consumption.

bands.label: Elevated
bands.reading: Sensitivity to income shocks rising. Marginal consumption starts to depend on credit.

bands.label: High
bands.reading: Debt service claims enough income that a labour market wobble transmits quickly to spending.

bands.label: Approaching the critical band
bands.reading: The last two visits to this level preceded consumer-led downturns.

bands.label: Critical
bands.reading: Household cash flow severely constrained. Recession amplifier.

bands.label: Peak-2007 territory
bands.reading: Deleveraging becomes involuntary. Consumption contracts regardless of policy.

sahmRealtime.note: Sahm rule, real-time vintage. Known false positive in 2024.

delinquencyAccel.note: 4-quarter change. Threshold = 90th percentile of its own history since 1987.

pillars.name: Cycle

band.label: Normalizing
band.reading: Post-inversion steepening — historically the phase immediately preceding recession onset, not an all-clear.

pillars.description: Yield curve spread between 10Y and 2Y Treasuries. Normalizing from inversion historically precedes credit stress by 6–18 months.

pillars.name: Liquidity

band.label: Extreme
band.reading: Top 5% of eighty years of history. Every prior visit to this band was followed by a major drawdown.

pillars.description: Buffett Indicator (Total US Corporate Equities / GDP) at 288.3% — 99.3th percentile vs. its own history since 1947-10-01 (302 quarters). Total corporate equities $91.9T vs. GDP $31.9T (quarter ending 2026-01-01). M2 YoY growth: +5.4%. Updates quarterly with each Fed Z.1 / BEA GDP release, not weekly — a change from the prior (non-functional) daily Wilshire proxy.

pillars.name: Premium

epAnchor.basis: earnings held from the reference date, price marked to the latest close

band.label: Negative
band.context: Equities yield less than the 10-year Treasury
band.reading: No compensation whatsoever for holding equity risk. The bond is the higher-yielding asset.

pillars.description: ERP = E/P (3.82%) minus the 10Y yield (4.78%). Earnings are held from the 2026-08-31 reference (3.84% E/P) and marked to the latest S&P 500 close, so the pillar moves with both the market and the 10Y. Aggregate earnings are updated by hand each quarter.

pillars.name: Solvency

band.label: Low
band.reading: Excellent credit quality. Banking plumbing unobstructed.

pillars.description: FRED DRALACBN delinquency rate at 1.38%. Systemic banking plumbing functioning normally.

pillars.name: Debt

band.label: Elevated
band.reading: Sensitivity to income shocks rising. Marginal consumption starts to depend on credit.

pillars.description: Household debt service ratio at 11.2%. Consumer balance sheet strain increasing.

sentinels.name: Initial Jobless Claims
sentinels.description: Weekly initial jobless claims at 206K. Red alert triggers above 275,000.

sentinels.name: Equity Risk Premium
sentinels.description: ERP at -0.96%. Red alert triggers below 0.80%.

sentinels.description: US unemployment rate at 4.1%. BDC stagflation stress trigger activates at 5.2%.
